job: Hold a place for content that is loading, with the same shape as the real thing.
purpose: Blocks with the exact geometry of what they stand in for, so the real content swaps in without a line moving. Parts: text lines, titles by type role, avatar, button, tile. Presets fill themselves from an empty element; fire-design/skeleton returns the same markup for static HTML. fd-skeleton-app is the first load. In a loading region a skeleton waits a moment before it shows.
useWhen: A region has a known layout and its data is on the way: the preset shaped like it, a table for a table, a list for a list.
The first load, before any script: fd-skeleton-app in the page's static HTML, with the shell's own geometry.
Moving between pages: the shell and the page head stay, and only the content region is a skeleton.
Content swaps in place: wrap skeleton and content in data-fd-loading and call setLoading(el, false).
A load can be slow: one fd-skeleton-late line in the loading region says so after a few seconds.

avoidWhen.when: A whole page drawn as a bare box of bars, with no shell and no page head.
avoidWhen.instead: Keep the shell and the head; use fd-skeleton-app on first load, or a preset in the content region

avoidWhen.when: A small control or one line of text.
The request failed; say what failed.
The page is empty on purpose.

states.name: loading
states.how: aria-busy="true" on the container; data-fd-loading="true" for a swap, shown after --fd-skeleton-delay

states.name: ready
states.how: setLoading(el, false); the skeleton fades and the content rises 8px

states.name: late
states.how: fd-skeleton-late shows after --fd-skeleton-late and is announced once; it goes when loading ends

states.name: stagger
states.how: --fd-i on a part staggers its shimmer
